title: Universal syntomic locus of a fixed relative dimension
statement: Let $g:P\to T$ be a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $d\geq0$ be an integer. A scheme locally of finite type over a field is a local complete intersection if it has an affine open cover by spectra of finitely generated local-complete-intersection algebras [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]. Call a scheme morphism syntomic if it is flat, locally of finite presentation and all its geometric fibres [def-weil-geometric-fibre] are local complete intersections. An open subscheme is given by an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. There is a largest open subscheme $L_d(g)\subseteq P$ on which $g$ is syntomic and every nonempty geometric fibre is pure of dimension $d$ [def-weil-pure-dimension]. Its formation commutes with arbitrary scheme base change: $L_d(g_{T'})=L_d(g)\times_TT'$ for every $T'\to T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. On a geometric fibre $C=P\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, where $\Omega$ is algebraically closed [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], $L_d(g)_\Omega$ is the union of all open subschemes of $C$ which are local complete intersections and pure of dimension $d$. It contains every point having a neighbourhood smooth of relative dimension $d$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For a closed point $c\in C$ [def-weil-closed-points], membership in $L_d(g)_\Omega$ is equivalent to its completed local $\Omega$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] being a complete intersection of Krull dimension $d$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Here a completed local $\Omega$-algebra is a complete intersection when it is isomorphic to $\Omega[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]/(h_1,\ldots,h_s)$ for some finite $r,s$, with the $h_i$ a regular sequence in the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series, def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Empty sources and fibres are allowed.

Geometric complete-intersection characterization: Tag 01UF (lemma-syntomic-flat-fibres). proof.text: We may restrict $g$ to a source open without losing flatness or local finite presentation: the local-ring maps are unchanged, and an affine presentation near a point can be restricted to a principal affine neighbourhood inside the open. Explicitly, replacing $B=A[z_1,\ldots,z_r]/(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$ by $B_b$ adds a variable $u$ and the single relation $ub-1$. A finite presentation is in particular a finite-type presentation, so $g$ is locally of finite type. For any base change $T'\to T$, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] show that $g_{T'}$ is again flat and locally of finite presentation. These observations apply also to geometric fibres and all subsequent source opens.

Apply [lem-trf-syntomic-locus-base-change] to obtain the open $V\subseteq P$ of points $x$ for which the local ring of $P_{g(x)}$ at $x$ is a complete-intersection local ring over $\kappa(g(x))$. It satisfies $V(g_{T'})=p^{-1}V(g)$ for the projection $p:P\times_TT'\to P$. By [lem-trf-lci-pointwise-criterion], the ordinary fibres of $V$ have the affine lci covers stated here. For $t\in T$ and its chosen algebraic closure, $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(t)}\to T$, the same equality of loci says that every local ring of the geometric fibre $V_{\bar t}$ is a complete-intersection local ring over $\overline{\kappa(t)}$; the same criterion gives an affine lci cover of $V_{\bar t}$, and likewise of $O_{\bar t}$ for every open $O\subseteq V$, whose local rings are among these. Conversely, suppose an open $W$ has lci geometric fibres, and take $x\in W$ with $t=g(x)$. The ring $\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(t)}\overline{\kappa(t)}$ is a tensor product of two nonzero vector spaces over a field, hence nonzero, so it has a prime ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] there is a point $x_1$ of $P_{\bar t}=P\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(t)}$ with $p(x_1)=x$; it lies in the open $W_{\bar t}=p^{-1}(W)$. Its local ring there, which is its local ring on $P_{\bar t}$, is a complete intersection over $\overline{\kappa(t)}$ by the local-ring criterion, so $x_1\in V(g_{\bar t})=p^{-1}V(g)$ and hence $x\in V(g)$. Thus $g|_V$ and its restrictions to source opens are syntomic in precisely the geometric-fibre definition stated here, and every syntomic source open lies in $V$.

Every ordinary fibre of $V\to T$ has an affine lci cover by step 2. At each $x\in V$, its fibre is an open of $P_{g(x)}$ and has the same local ring at $x$. Thus [lem-sfb-lci-cohen-macaulay-stalks] gives depth equal to Krull dimension at every one of its points, including nonclosed points. Apply [lem-sbc-cohen-macaulay-equidimensional-fibre-pieces] with source $P$, base open $T$ and source open $W=V$. It gives pairwise disjoint opens $V_n$ covering $V$, such that every nonempty fibre of $V_n\to T$ is pure of dimension $n$. By [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension], for $x\in V_n$ the local topological dimension of the original fibre $P_{g(x)}$ at $x$ is $n$. Write this dimension as $\nu_g(x)$. As the $V_n$ cover $V$, each $V_n$ is exactly $\{x\in V:\nu_g(x)=n\}$. Define $L_d(g)=V_d$. In particular it is an open of $P$, and its ordinary nonempty fibres are pure of dimension $d$.

proof.text: Let $T'\to T$ be arbitrary and let $x'\in P'=P\times_TT'$ map to $x\in P$, with base points $t'$ and $t$. The fibre through $x'$ is $P_t\times_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(t')$. On an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}S$ of $x$ in $P_t$, the algebra $S$ is finite type over $\kappa(t)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs]. The inverse-image chart is $\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(t'))$; the prime for $x'$ contracts to the prime for $x$ under $s\mapsto s\otimes1$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-field-extension] to these primes gives $\nu_{g_{T'}}(x')=\nu_g(x)$; taking the affine neighbourhood does not change local topological dimension, since neighbourhoods contained in an open form a cofinal neighbourhood family. By step 2, $x'$ belongs to $V(g_{T'})$ exactly when $x\in V(g)$. Using the description of $V_d$ in step 3 on both schemes gives $x'\in L_d(g_{T'})$ exactly when $x\in L_d(g)$. The opens are therefore equal. Under the canonical fibre-product identification of inverse-image opens this is $L_d(g_{T'})=L_d(g)\times_TT'$.

The restriction to the open $L_d(g)\subseteq V$ is syntomic by step 2. Its ordinary fibres are pure of dimension $d$ by step 3, so [lem-trf-relative-dimension-base-change] shows that its geometric fibres are pure of dimension $d$ as well. For maximality, let $W\subseteq P$ be any open with the two required geometric-fibre properties. Step 2 gives $W\subseteq V$. For $x\in W$ with $t=g(x)$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] gives, as in step 2, a point $x_1$ of the geometric fibre $W_{\bar t}$ over the chosen $\overline{\kappa(t)}$ with $p(x_1)=x$. The open $W_{\bar t}$ of $P_{\bar t}$ is nonempty and pure of dimension $d$, so [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension] gives $\dim_{x_1}(P_{\bar t})=d$. Take an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}S$ of $x$ in $P_t$, with $S$ finite type over $\kappa(t)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs]. Then $x_1$ lies in the open $\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_{\kappa(t)}\overline{\kappa(t)})$ of $P_{\bar t}$, as a prime lying over the prime of $x$. The equality in [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-field-extension], with local dimension unchanged on passing to an open as in step 4, gives $\nu_g(x)=d$. Thus $x\in V_d$, proving $W\subseteq L_d(g)$.

proof.text: For a geometric fibre $C=P\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, step 4 identifies $L_d(g)_\Omega$ with $L_d(C\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)$. The latter is itself an open lci scheme, pure of dimension $d$, by steps 2, 3 and 5. Conversely, if $O\subseteq C$ is any open lci scheme pure of dimension $d$, then $O\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is an open restriction of the geometric base change of the original flat, locally finitely presented $g$. Thus step 1 supplies both properties; flatness is inherited from $g$, without a new assumption on $O$. By [lem-trf-lci-pointwise-criterion] every local ring of $O$ is a complete intersection. Its locus in [lem-trf-syntomic-locus-base-change] is therefore all of $O$, and stays all of the source after any geometric base change; applying the local-ring criterion again makes those fibres lci. Its pure-dimensional ordinary fibre remains pure of dimension $d$ under every field extension by [lem-trf-relative-dimension-base-change]. Hence maximality from step 5 gives $O\subseteq L_d(C\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)$. Since this open is one of the $O$ under consideration, it is exactly their union.

source.place: Tags 02V3, 01UG, 01UF and 02NK; identification of the geometric-fibre open

proof.text: Suppose $x$ has an open neighbourhood $H\subseteq P$ on which $g$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], every geometric fibre of $H\to T$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$ over its algebraically closed base field, so is pure of dimension $d$ by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For such a smooth fibre, [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-regularity-smooth-field-criterion], taking the identity field extension, says every local ring is regular. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], it is also essentially of finite type over the field: it is a localization of a finite-type affine coordinate algebra. Such a regular local algebra is a complete-intersection local algebra by using its identity quotient and the empty regular sequence. The local-ring criterion [lem-trf-lci-pointwise-criterion] therefore gives an affine lci cover of that fibre. Step 1 supplies flatness and local finite presentation of $g|_H$, so $H$ has both properties in step 5 and $x\in H\subseteq L_d(g)$.

Fix a closed point $c$ of the geometric fibre $C$ and an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}S\subseteq C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], $S$ is a finitely generated $\Omega$-algebra. Closedness of $c$ makes its prime $\mathfrak m$ maximal. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $A=\mathcal O_{C,c}=S_{\mathfrak m}$. The residue-field result [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] identifies $S/\mathfrak m$ with $\Omega$ via its given structural map, not an unspecified field isomorphism. Apply [lem-trf-separable-closed-point-formal-presentation] to $k=F=\Omega$ (the identity extension is finite separable). It gives Noetherian local rings $A,\widehat A$ and a surjection of $\Omega$-algebras $\Phi:Q=\Omega[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]\twoheadrightarrow\widehat A$, with kernel in $(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$. The $\Omega$-action is the original one: the $\Omega$-algebra section of the residue map is forced to be the structural map when $F=\Omega$.

source.place: varieties.tex Tag 0C52 (lemma-complete-local-ring-structure-as-algebra), separable case; algebra.tex Tag 00FV; schemes.tex Tag 01HV

proof.text: If $c$ belongs to the syntomic open $V(C\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)$, then $A$ is a complete-intersection local $\Omega$-algebra. By [lem-trf-lci-pointwise-criterion], write $A\cong R/I$ as a $\Omega$-algebra, where $R$ is regular local, essentially of finite type over $\Omega$, and $I$ is generated by a finite regular sequence. Since $A=S_{\mathfrak m}$ has residue field $\Omega$, it is nonzero. Hence $I$ is proper and lies in the unique maximal ideal of $R$, as required by the kernel test. The isomorphism $A\cong R/I$ identifies the unique maximal ideals, hence their powers and the quotients by those powers. Taking their inverse limits identifies $\widehat A$ with $\widehat{R/I}$ as $\Omega$-algebras. Via this identification, $\Phi$ is the surjection onto the completion of $R/I$ required below. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete], the source $Q$ of $\Phi$ in step 8 is regular local. Apply [lem-trf-regular-quotient-completion-kernel-test] to $R,I,Q,\Phi$. It says that $\ker\Phi$ is generated by a finite $Q$-regular sequence $h_1,\ldots,h_s$ in the maximal ideal. Since $\Phi$ respects $\Omega$, its quotient isomorphism $Q/(h_1,\ldots,h_s)\cong\widehat A$ respects $\Omega$ as well. Conversely, an isomorphism of completed local $\Omega$-algebras to a finite-variable power series quotient by a regular sequence in its maximal ideal is in particular a ring isomorphism. By [lem-trf-completion-local-complete-intersection], applied to $S,\mathfrak m$, it gives a principal affine lci neighbourhood of $c$. The local-ring criterion then gives that $A$ is a complete-intersection local $\Omega$-algebra, so $c\in V(C\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)$. This proves the equivalence while retaining the coefficient-algebra structure in the forward direction.

At the closed point $c$, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-dimension-local-ring] applied on $U$ gives $\nu_{C\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega}(c)=\dim A$: passing to the open $U$ does not change local dimension. Since $A$ is Noetherian local by step 8, [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension-eq] gives $\dim A=\dim\widehat A$. Together with the pointwise description $L_d=\{c\in V:\nu(c)=d\}$ in step 3 and the equivalence in step 9, this proves exactly that $c\in L_d(g)_\Omega$ if and only if $\widehat A$ is a complete-intersection completed local $\Omega$-algebra of Krull dimension $d$. All constructions and arguments include the empty source or an empty fibre: the partitions and loci there are empty, the empty scheme has pure dimension $d$ by [def-weil-pure-dimension], and the closed-point clauses have no instances. Empty regular sequences are allowed, so the regular and dimension-zero cases have not been excluded.
